question:
A 48-year-old woman is referred to an orthopedic surgeon by her primary care physician due to a
10-year history of right knee osteoarthritis. Over the past 6 months, she has been unable to walk her
dog due to severe pain that worsens with movement, and in recent weeks, she has also experienced
pain at night without movement. Her medical history includes multiple knee injuries from playing soccer
in college. Previous treatments, including physical therapy, diclofenac, and intraarticular glucocorticoid
injections, have failed to provide significant relief. She has no other significant medical history. Her
height is 164 cm (5 ft 4 in), weight is 74 kg (163 lb), and BMI is 28 kg/m². Examination reveals limited
range of motion in the right knee, palpable crepitus, and moderate swelling. X-rays of the right knee
show significant osteophyte formation and irregular joint space narrowing. The surgeon proposes
scheduling a total knee arthroplasty. The patient has HMO insurance, and the surgeon is an in-network
provider. She expresses concern about potential out-of-pocket costs for this procedure. What is the
most appropriate administrative step for the orthopedic surgeon to take? Answer Choices: (A) Require
the patient to pay in full before scheduling the surgery (B) Defer knee surgery until a request for
reimbursement is approved by the HMO (C) Suggest the patient consider alternative therapies to avoid
high out-of-pocket costs (D) Proceed with the surgery and bill the patient directly for any uncovered
costs (E) Ask the patient to seek approval from the HMO for reimbursement prior to surgery (F)
Perform the knee surgery and then submit a reimbursement claim to the HMO (G) Request a
preauthorization directly from the HMO before scheduling the surgery (H) Recommend postponing
surgery until the patient changes to a different insurance plan (I) Refer the patient to a financial
counselor to discuss payment options (J) Submit an expedited claim to the HMO for retroactive
approval after the surgery
 A. Ask the patient to seek approval from the HMO for reimbursement prior to surgery
B. Require the patient to pay in full before scheduling the surgery

C. Recommend postponing surgery until the patient changes to a different insurance plan
D. Perform the knee surgery and then submit a reimbursement claim to the HMO
E. Submit an expedited claim to the HMO for retroactive approval after the surgery
F. Request a preauthorization directly from the HMO before scheduling the surgery
G. Defer knee surgery until a request for reimbursement is approved by the HMO
H. Suggest the patient consider alternative therapies to avoid high out-of-pocket costs
I. Proceed with the surgery and bill the patient directly for any uncovered costs
J. Refer the patient to a financial counselor to discuss payment options
